payload.title: g1_gap_free_run returns only the longest gap-free run of the whole history, never the current trailing run, so a gate written as run >= consecutive_cycles stays satisfied forever after 14 good cycles followed by any number of cycles with no report

payload.rule_violated: PLAN-v2 section 4, G1: '14 consecutive cycles, every field measured' is about the cycles up to now; a reader of a pre-registered gate must expose what the gate decides on.
payload.notes: History: 14 gap-free cycles, then 30 cycles with no report. The loop sets run to 0 on each missing report but longest stays 14, so the reader returns run 14 and names first_gap at the 15th cycle (read from the loop; the review's probe_b reports the same). Any consumer that compares run with the pre-registered consecutive_cycles (14) passes the gate on a stale run, although no cycle of the last 30 was measured. The spec says 'longest run', but the gate it feeds needs the trailing one, which the same loop already computes. Close condition: Return the trailing run beside the longest (a current_run key) and document which one a gate must read; a test with 14 good cycles followed by one missing report asserts current_run is 0 while the longest stays 14. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
